comment: Eight review-account runs (003-010), all inside the encoded domain and scored against P-0036 model.py with review_error. Seven are at the noise floor (judged RMSE/L 0.0049-0.0052): A-B at r0 3.5, 4.0, 5.0; A-C at 4.0 and 5.0; B-C at 3.0 and 4.0. Run 006 (A-B, r0 3.0, horizontal, T 2) scores 4.03. Observed and model separations agree to t about 1.4. The observed pair then reaches contact (observed minimum separation about 0.2 at t 1.6) and rebounds to 1.7 by t 2. The model has no contact rule and blows up after t 1.6 (r^-2.5 pass-through). Verdict narrowed, not falsified: 7 of 8 in-domain runs pass, so the failure is a close-approach limit, not a wrong law. The encoded domain (r 3 to 5, T <= 2, no contact limit) admits contact runs. Proposed domain r 4 to 5: A-B at r0 4.0 keeps model separation at or above 2.4 over T 2, and run 003 passes there. This also excludes run 007 (A-B, r0 3.5), which passes but approaches to about 0.7 observed. The domain format cannot express T or contact limits, so please read the contact exclusion as part of the narrowed claim.
